desc: Analyze the problem structure: $x_j=1$ iff $j \in \bigcup_{i \in I_1} [L_i, R_i] \cup \bigcap_{i \in I_2} [L_i, R_i]^c$. Condition for all 1s: $\bigcap_{i \in I_2} [L_i, R_i] \subseteq \bigcup_{i \in I_1} [L_i, R_i]$.
Identify key cases: $I_2 = \emptyset$ (cover $[1,N]$), $I_2$ has empty intersection (cost 2), $I_2=\{k\}$ (cover $[L_k, R_k]$ with others), $I_2=\{j,k\}$ with non-empty intersection.
Implement `min_cover(start, end, exclude_set)` using a greedy approach with precomputed structures (sorted intervals, max R array, binary search) to handle exclusions efficiently.
Check Case 1: Cover $[1, N]$ with no exclusions.
Check Case 2: Find if any pair of intervals has empty intersection. If so, cost 2 is possible.
Check Case 3: For each interval $k$, check if $[L_k, R_k]$ can be covered by all intervals except $k$. Cost $1 + \text{cover}$.

Check Case 4: If no better solution found, check if any pair $j,k$ has non-empty intersection $[A,B]$ and $[A,B]$ can be covered by others. Cost $2 + \text{cover}$. Note: If all pairs intersect, the global intersection is non-empty.
Reconstruct the optimal solution and print the output.
